Lead source: inbound self-serve sign-up (site contact form). Small, family-run specialty goods marketplace focused on curated home accessories. Typical traffic: steady daily shoppers, big bursts during weekend drops and holiday promos.

Discovery notes:
- Interested in Hosted API (self-serve). Wants fast time-to-implement; minimal infra.
- Primary problems: product page Q&A (answer specs, care instructions), automated attribute extraction for new vendor SKUs, lightweight search re-ranking.
- Quote from founder (Elena): 'We need answers on product pages that don't feel generic — and it has to be cheap.'
- Cost sensitivity: high. Willing to use smaller models for low-cost responses, but needs quality fallback for ambiguous queries.
- Latency target: page-level Q&A <200ms p50, acceptable p95 up to 400ms for cold calls.
- Throughput: baseline ~5-15 rps; promo peaks 50-120 rps for 5-8 hour windows.
- Model preference: open/commercial mix — start with a smaller open model (cost control) + staged fallback to larger when needed. Wants easy model pinning and routing.
- Caching: interested in prefix/KV caching for product descriptions and common Qs to save cost and hit latency.
- Data handling: cannot retain customer PII; wants auto-delete option (30d) and exportable logs for audits.

Technical bits from call:
- Frontend: Next.js storefront + Algolia currently for baseline search.
- Backend: Node.js microservices on Vercel for frontend and a small Heroku/managed DB. Prefer minimal infra changes.
- Integration ask: SDK example for Node, easy token rotation, example prompt templates for product Q&A and attribute extraction.
